display.title: Toldos: The Little Yaakov and the Little Esav Inside Us
display.summary_short: Everyone has a little Yaakov and a little Esav inside. Like a seesaw, every mitzvah makes the yetzer tov stronger and the yetzer hara weaker.
display.summary_long: A parsha talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show for Parshas Toldos. Yaakov sat in the tents learning Torah and behaving well, while his brother Esav was always outside looking for trouble. Our Sages teach that each of us has a little Yaakov, the yetzer tov, and a little Esav, the yetzer hara. Uncle Yossi compares them to a seesaw: every mitzvah lifts Yaakov up and pushes Esav down. The way to win the war is to ignore the yetzer hara and answer every temptation with a mitzvah: say the Shema or one of the Twelve Pesukim, put a coin in the pushka, honor parents, or do a kindness. Eventually the yetzer hara gives up, and that is what it means to be a tzaddik. It takes time, but before birth every soul is told to be a tzaddik and is given the strength to do it. When Moshiach comes, all evil will disappear, and we will go joyfully to Eretz Yisroel and the third Beis HaMikdash.
display.lesson: Ignore the yetzer hara and answer it with a mitzvah; every mitzvah makes your inner Yaakov stronger.
